==Problem==
Brynn's savings decreased by <imath>20 \%</imath> in July, then increased by <imath>50 \%</imath> in August. Brynn's savings are now what percent of the original amount?

<imath>\textbf{(A)}\ 80 \qquad \textbf{(B)}\ 90 \qquad \textbf{(C)}\ 100 \qquad \textbf{(D)}\ 110 \qquad \textbf{(E)}\ 120</imath>

==Solution 1==
Let <imath>x</imath> be Byron's original amount. We see that Byron had <imath>0.8x</imath> in July. Then, he increased his savings by HALF of how much he had as of July which is <imath>0.4x</imath>. Adding <imath>0.4x + 0.8x</imath>, we get <imath>1.2x</imath>, so his August savings are <imath>\boxed{ \textbf{(E) } 120 }\%</imath> of <imath>x</imath>. 

~Ingeniouspeacock36

We see that the change is <imath>(1-0.2)(1+0.5) = 0.8 \cdot 1.5 = 1.2</imath>. That is an increase of <imath>20\%</imath>, so his August savings are <imath>\boxed{ \textbf{(E) } 120 }\%</imath> of his original savings.

~OlympiadMaster

==Solution 2==

Let's assume Brynn has <imath>\$100</imath> at the start. In July, he lost <imath>20\%</imath>, so he lost <imath>\$20</imath>, so he has <imath>100-20=80</imath> dollars left. <imath>50</imath> percent of <imath>80</imath> dollars is <imath>40</imath> dollars, so he gained <imath>40</imath> dollars in August, so now he has <imath>80+40=120</imath> dollars, which is <imath>120\%</imath> of <imath>100</imath> dollars, so our answer is <imath>\boxed{ \textbf{(E) } 120 }\% </imath>.

~Yuhao2012

We can also do it just with percentages. He has <imath>100\%</imath> then loses <imath>20\%</imath>, meaning he now has <imath>80\%</imath>. Then he gains <imath>50</imath> percent of our NEW amount (which is <imath>80</imath> percent) and <imath>50</imath> percent of <imath>80</imath> is <imath>40</imath> percent, so we add <imath>40</imath> and <imath>80</imath> to get our answer, <imath>\boxed{ \textbf{(E) } 120 }\% </imath>.

~pereena

You can also do it with fractions. You can say you have <imath>\frac{100}{100}</imath> at the beginning, then losing <imath>20\%</imath> would result in <imath>\frac{80}{100}</imath>. <imath>50\%</imath> of <imath>\frac{80}{100}</imath> is <imath>\frac{40}{100}</imath>. Adding <imath>\frac{40}{100}</imath> to the original <imath>\frac{80}{100}</imath> gives <imath>\frac{120}{100}</imath>, which is <imath>\boxed{ \textbf{(E) } 120 }\% </imath> of <imath>\frac{100}{100}</imath>.

~Broie, fixed fraction by anabel.disher

==Solution 3==

Let Brynn's savings be <imath> x </imath>. Then, in July from <imath> x </imath> his savings went down <imath> x - \frac{1}{5}x = \frac{4}{5}x </imath>. From that amount, it increased <imath>50\%</imath> in August, meaning we have <imath> \frac{8}{10}x + \frac{4}{10}x = \frac{12}{10}x = \frac{6}{5}x </imath> remaining. Of the total <imath> x </imath>, which is <imath> \frac{\frac{6}{5}x}{x} </imath>, we see that the <imath> x </imath> cancel out and the increase is <imath> \frac{6}{5} </imath>, or <imath> \boxed{120} </imath>%

~Pinotation (your so tuff ~ jimmy_io) (ty bro <3 ~Pinotation)
